en: This merciless melon demolisher is a menace for all aspiring gardeners.
These grapes must pack a punch, if this little owl had feasted on them so viciously.
This mushroom is moving on its own! Just what are they putting in that Spring Water…?
Already matured, yet still somehow miniscule. Going fast and strong nevertheless.
Angry and all out of honey. Not a good combination.

It wants to aggressively peck at your feet. A true killing machine is about to be let loose.
You almost mistook this serpent for a twig! Luckily your keen eye caught the difference before your axe could.
The steady buzzing of this insect could drive a short-tempered to insanity.
Comes with bite sized candy. Experts advise against eating them.
Just a simple touch and it scurries back into your pocket.
Curious and chatty, at night and at day. You wonder how it survived for so long on its own.
This bat has no visible eyes, yet can maneuver effortlessly through the air.
Simian real estate is scarce in today's times, especially with people chopping trees left and right. You wouldn't leave this little fellow all alone, would you?
It is well known that the buccaneers of the South Seas keep parrots as their companions, but not many know that there are educated trainers preparing them for long days at sea.
A sluggish gelatinous wanderer, feeding on rot and leaving a glistening trail of decay behind.
The silk of this moth glitters in the moonlight like a curtain of endless stars.
Some of the Sawtooth offspring have found their way into the care of the Sanv Tribe, now being trained to be protectors of the Harborage.
It speaks in an alien language.
